section_summary: This section covers diplomatic correspondence and administrative directives from March to December 1946 regarding travel, entry, exit, and quarantine regulations for occupied Japan. Due to acute shortages of food and housing, SCAP and the State Department strictly limited entry permits primarily to official occupation personnel and missionaries, consistently denying or postponing applications from commercial businessmen and trade missions. Key documents establish procedures for registering approved non-Japanese residents (SCAPIN-852), control of individuals, aircraft, and surface vessels (Circular No. 8), and comprehensive maritime and aerial foreign quarantine regulations (Circular No. 10).

subfiles.about: Establishes comprehensive quarantine procedures, inspection standards, and sanitary controls for all individuals, vessels, and aircraft entering or leaving Japan.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Promulgates comprehensive foreign quarantine regulations for Japan under SCAP authority, covering the four main islands and occupied outlying islands. The circular prescribes detailed inspection, disinfestation, vaccination, and clearance procedures for incoming and outgoing aircraft, surface vessels, passengers, cargo, and animals. It designates quarantine enforcement to the Eighth Army and specifies controls for quarantinable diseases including cholera, plague, smallpox, typhus, and yellow fever.
subfiles.title: SCAP Circular No. 10: Foreign Quarantine Regulations for Japan
